alternatives.labelRationale: Foundations in biodiversity, history and philosophy support conservation and later work on climate and environmental governance. Statistics, data analysis and qualitative methods support documentary and historical research.

alternatives.concept: Study how biological systems, brains and behaviour shape health. Build from cell biology, neuroscience and psychology to physiology, immunology, disease mechanisms, mental health and research synthesis.

alternatives.labelRationale: The life science and brain and behaviour gateways precede laboratory biology, psycholinguistics, neuroscience and health courses. Statistics supports the later systematic review and meta-analysis course.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Biomedical science and cognitive and health research replace the general option’s concentration on history, institutions, culture and environmental challenges.

alternatives.concept: Study how institutions govern markets and societies. Combine political philosophy, law, international relations and history with economics, company finance, cross-border business law and the effects of AI on businesses and labour markets.

alternatives.labelRationale: Introductory economics, politics, law and research methods support macroeconomics, microeconomics, public economics, econometrics and international and EU law. Company finance and the economics of AI add business applications.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Economics, finance and political and legal institutions take priority over environmental science or biomedical and cognitive study.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest option owns interdisciplinary breadth, research and societal challenges. Health and human behaviour, and institutions and markets, each support a distinct 180 EC UCR option. The business courses cover accounting, finance, entrepreneurship, cross-border business law and effects of AI adoption, with limited international management. Arts and Culture, human-centred AI and the Venice double-degree interest remain separate directions after three feasible options.

notes.text: Groningen requires a shared academic core, a major, a minor, three annual projects and a thesis. UCR students combine 24 courses in an open curriculum. Personal & Professional Development is required and independent research is optional.

audience.programmeDescription: University College Groningen offers an English-language degree in Liberal Arts and Sciences. This example uses the Free Major, which lets students combine humanities, social sciences and sciences while completing a common core and a minor.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines social and cultural study with ecology and climate science. Two further options concentrate on health and behaviour or on institutions and markets. Groningen has a separate project each year and a required thesis.
